newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Tight supply seen pushing prices up.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Tight supply seen pushing prices up.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to remain steady to higher this week due to tight supply from the Philippines, traders said.

"Copra supply in the market remains low. We don't expect any relief until the second quarter so expect prices to remain at this level or higher," said one trader with one of the country's largest coconut millers.
The trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines (UCAP) said coconut oil exports reached 39,060 tonnes from January 1 to 14.
Exports in January 1996 had reached 74,074 tonnes.
Traders said there were more paper transactions since last week rather than firm commitments to physically deliver the coconut oil or copra due to speculation on the supply from the Philippines.
"There are more CIF plays, or futures transactions, as supply from the Philippines does not warrant an FOB play," said another trader.
CIF refers to deals that include cost, insurance and freight while FOB are free-on-board transactions.

Last week, UCAP said coconut oil prices were slightly up with the average at $766.25 per tonne CIF against the previous week's average of $766 per tonne. There was no report of done deals on FOB basis, it said.
Traders attributed the slight increase to fears of a rise in corn and soybean prices due to lower than expected crop output in the United States last year.
Coconut oil supply from the Philippines, the world's largest exporter of the commodity, is expected to ease in the second quarter, traders said.
UCAP said earlier it expected coconut oil exports from the Philippines this year to reach 1.429 million tonnes in copra terms from the 1996 estimate of 1.333 million.
Coconut oil exports in copra terms in 1995 reached 2.118 million tonnes.
UCAP attributed the plunge in coconut oil exports from the Philippines last year to the effects of the devastation wrought by typhoons in coconut growing areas.

Traders pegged coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam at 25,000 tonnes on January 13. "There was oil for the immediate pipeline last week, but I don't know if there's enough left this week," one trader said.
Coconut oil stocks this week is expected to be lower in Rotterdam and the United States if there are no fresh supplies from the Philippines and Indonesia, they said.
The monthly coconut oil requirement in Rotterdam was placed at between 45,000 and 55,000 tonnes and between 40,000 and 45,000 tonnes in the United States.
Traders said they were still waiting for updates on whether the two boats that were expected to arrive in Rotterdan in the next two weeks are on schedule.

MV Blue Sapphire, with a cargo of 20,000 tonnes, is expected to arrive between January 15 and 30 while MV Auriga, with a cargo of 16,000 tonnes, is expected to arrive later this month to early February, they said earlier.

"The ball game is on the consumers this week. If they come out to buy more oils then prices will go up. But if consumers feel that there is nothing to worry and supply from the Philippines would eventually ease then it can go down, but not as much," a trader said.
